title: TenantAnchorRecord
description: The persisted form of a run's tenant anchor record (ADR 0065, the normative tenant-anchor specification): the tenant-held high-water mark the control plane cannot rewrite, and the write-ahead log that makes an honest crash recoverable. One record per run, in a store only the tenant can write, replaced whole under compare-and-swap by exactly the acceptance predicate.

runId.description: The run this record anchors. Immutable across every write.

environmentId.description: The environment the run is pinned to. Immutable across every write.

state.description: Whether the run is still advancing, or closed. A terminal record refuses every claim.

disposition.description: How a terminal record was closed: by its terminal checkpoint, or by an operator-signed abandonment that discarded an outstanding staged save. None while live.

epochHighWater.description: The highest ordering key ever accepted for this run. Raised by any accepted write to the key it carries, lowered only by a re-anchor.

committed.description: The last checkpoint the tenant committed to.

pending.description: The staged next checkpoint, when a save is in flight. Absent otherwise.

reanchorCounter.description: Strictly monotonic; a re-anchor increments it, which is what stops a signed re-anchor being replayed. A record recovered from a lost anchor starts at 1, which also distinguishes that recovery from a fresh create.

OrderingKey.title: OrderingKey
OrderingKey.description: An (incarnation, epoch) pair compared lexicographically. An incarnation change resets the control plane's epoch counter, so epochs are not comparable across one.

incarnation.description: The tenant-attested store incarnation the key was written under.

epoch.description: The lease epoch the control plane minted for the grant.

Mark.title: Mark
Mark.description: A committed or pending mark: a checkpoint's identity at an ordering key.

key.description: The ordering key the mark was written under.

digest.description: The checkpoint digest over the pinned submitted-bytes layout: 32 bytes, base64.
